bench-baseline-loose-rot-is-silent: Bench baselines rot in BOTH directions, and only one direction is self-announcing. A baseline that is too TIGHT fails the gate and gets fixed immediately; a baseline that is too LOOSE is silent — the bench just passes, and the slack hides real regressions. Before angr-xvinq (2026-07-13) sharif7_rev50 ran at 0.21x of its baseline, so a 4x regression would have passed the 15% gate unnoticed; 7 other fast-tier entries sat at 0.64-0.82x. Standing rule: whenever you refresh baseline_timings.json for a drift FAILURE, also scan the whole suite for entries where max-observed/baseline < 0.85 and lower those in the same pass. Method: run run_regression.py --rust-only --skip-bimodal N>=6 times, parse the per-bench 'Rust: X.XXs' lines (headers are '--- name ---', DFS twins '--- name (DFS) ---' -> key name__dfs), take max-of-N as the new rust_time. max-of-N not median: it leaves the 15% threshold as headroom above the slowest observed run, so the gate is sensitive without flapping. Leave entries in the 0.85-1.0 band alone (ais3_crackme) — too close to noise to tighten safely. Write back with json.dump(..., indent=2, sort_keys=False) to preserve insertion order (see bench-baseline-dfs-variant-key). SINCE angr-z8p3x (2026-08-09) the effective headroom is max(threshold*baseline, --regression-floor) with the floor defaulting to 50ms (run_regression.timing_regression_pct) — so on the sub-second benches tightening a baseline below ~0.33s buys NO extra sensitivity past the 50ms floor, and the smallest real regression the gate can catch there is 50ms, not 15%.
bench-pin-derive-from-gate-log-percentil: Deriving a PINNED_RUST_TIMES value: mine the per-bench in-gate timings out of .ralph/state/logs/*gate-stdout.txt rather than re-running the bench. Each gate stdout has a '--- <bench> ---' block followed by a 'Rust:   N.NNs' line; ~2000 samples are on disk, so sorting the last 300 by mtime gives real p50/p95/p99/max for that bench under gate conditions (loaded 6G scope, right after 'cargo test --release'), which standalone run_single.py reads systematically understate. DECISION RULE: compare the current 15%% bar (baseline*1.15) against that distribution and count exceedances. p50 still at the baseline + a few percent of runs over the bar = load-sensitive tail, so pin (this is what ais3_crackme's 3.3%% was, angr-pj6bt; cmu_binary_bomb_partial's was 3.7%%, angr-97aww). p50 itself shifted = real regression, do NOT pin. Around 1%% exceedance, decline to pin and say so on the bead — --retry-failures already covers it and a pin costs detection power (unmapped_analysis, 1.3%%). Pick the pin so its bar clears every read of the incident that motivated it and ~299/300 samples; state the resulting detection threshold (p50+30%% is the range the three existing pins landed in), and add a test_timing_gate.py case asserting those exact reads clear. Pair with avoid-update-clobbering-pinned-baselines: the pin must be written to BOTH PINNED_RUST_TIMES and baseline_timings.json (test_live_pin_matches_the_checked_in_baseline enforces it).
benchmark-regression-noise-floor:
Benchmark regression --threshold 0.15 on the sub-second smoke benches (arm_le_branch, mips64_le_branch, ais3_crackme, defcamp_r100, unbreakable_0) is noise-dominated: any single run can flag 3-4 'failures' that swap each run. Confirmed 2026-05-25 (angr-kwpi.1): same diff produced 4/15 fail, then 3/15 fail with different bench set, then 0/15 fail on the next run, with no changes between runs. RULE: a single failing benchmark gate run is not a real regression — re-run at least once; only believe the gate if the SAME bench fails twice in SEPARATE runs. Real regressions also typically exceed 25-30% on the slow-tier benches, not just clip past 15% on smoke benches.

Slow-tier single-shot noise (merged from bench-noise-single-shot): even slow-tier single-shot run_regression.py results can show 15-22% regressions that vanish under a 5-sample median (within 2%). Confirm a suspected regression with: 'for i in 1 2 3 4 5; do python tests/benchmarks/run_single.py <bench> --engine rust 2>&1 | grep ^OK; done'. cmu_binary_bomb_partial: 1.62s one-shot vs 1.36s median (baseline 1.33s, within noise). Re-running run_regression.py once also usually confirms a noise spike.

In-gate retries are NOT independent samples (angr-mc8pw, 2026-08-09): --retry-failures re-runs immediately, inside the same contention window, so a host-contention excursion fails every attempt. ralph iter24 red on cow_fork_scaling at 3.09s/2.50s with retries at 3.11s and 3.37s; standalone re-runs minutes later were 2.45-2.48s. So 'failed twice' only counts across separate gate invocations.

FIRST DIAGNOSTIC on any gate red — was the HOST slow, or the bench? Two signals in the gate output itself: (1) the 'Total time:' line, normally 31-35s for the fast tier, was 47.4s on that run; (2) the median per-bench current/baseline ratio, 1.083x there, i.e. every bench shifted, not one. run_regression.py now computes (2) itself and normalizes timing failures by it before retrying (suite_median_ratio / host_scale_factor, dead-band 1.02x, cap 1.25x), so a red that survives normalization is materially more trustworthy than a pre-2026-08-09 one — but still re-run before bisecting.
